subject: Service availability guardrails & remediation cap proposal
messages:
From: Elena Park <elena.park@statelyfinance.com>
To: Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 25 May 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Request: availability carveouts and monthly remediation cap

Hi Monica,

Thanks again for the demo last week — the runtime looks promising for our end-of-month batch pipeline. Before we get too deep into procurement, our security and ops teams flagged two items in the standard SLA that we'd like Redwood to review:

1) Uptime target — we typically require 99.95% for production services with financial transaction dependencies. Can Redwood move from 99.9% to 99.95% for our account?

2) Monthly remediation credits — because our workflows include a scheduled 6–8 hour nightly batch window (Saturday), we need clear carveouts and an upper cap on monthly credits so accounting can model cost. The procurement team would prefer a predictable monthly cap rather than an open-ended remediation liability.

Attached is a short PDF that outlines the internal risk assessment and what Stately is asking for (stately_sla_request.pdf).

Also, latency matters for our reconciliation endpoint: we expect P95 under 300ms for the /reconcile route during business hours. Is that something Redwood can commit to (or measure and report)?

Can we schedule a quick call this week with procurement and legal?

Best,
Elena Park
Director, Platform Operations
Stately Finance
elena.park@statelyfinance.com

--
Attachment: stately_sla_request.pdf (summary of requested exceptions and justifications)

From: Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.ai>
To: Elena Park <elena.park@statelyfinance.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>, Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 25 May 2027 13:03:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Request: availability carveouts and monthly remediation cap

Elena —

Appreciate the clear ask and the PDF. Quick summary of Redwood's starting position and some initial remedies we can propose:

- Baseline hosted SLA: 99.9% monthly availability (standard).
- We can explore a 99.95% target for accounts with reserved capacity or a committed consumption tier. If Stately is willing to discuss Reserved/Dedicated sizing, we can price that separately.
- Monthly remediation: we typically cap credits as a percentage of the monthly invoice. As a first pass, Redwood is open to a capped monthly remediation amount (we propose 10% of monthly spend as a conversation starter).
- Maintenance carveouts: we can carve out scheduled batch windows (e.g., your Saturday 6–8 hour window) provided Redwood receives notification 72 hours prior and maintenance is limited in-hours for those windows.
- Latency: we can instrument P95 for the /reconcile route and include it in a route-level SLO dashboard. Committing to a hard P95 number requires us to align on traffic profile and whether caching/batching behavior is acceptable.

Attached is a short draft proposal (slo-offset-proposal-v1.pdf) that maps your asks to potential guardrails and next steps. For procurement/legal, looping in Laura (contracts) and Ben (reliability/pricing) — Laura/Ben, any redlines you want up front?

Next steps: 1) Can Elena share the expected monthly token/embedding volume and preferred deployment mode? 2) I'll schedule a 30-min alignment with procurement & legal.

Thanks,
Monica Patel
Enterprise Sales
Redwood Inference

Attachment: slo-offset-proposal-v1.pdf (internal draft mapping requests to options)

From: Elena Park <elena.park@statelyfinance.com>
To: Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.ai>
Cc: procurement@statelyfinance.com
Date: Wed, 26 May 2027 10:45:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Request: availability carveouts and monthly remediation cap

Monica —

Thanks for the quick turn. A few clarifications from procurement/ops:

- Stately is evaluating both Hosted and Dedicated; committed spend estimate is $120k/month initially, rising to $220k/month in 9 months.
- Procurement prefers a deterministic monthly cap on remediation (predictability > lowest possible cap). Open to % of invoice but would like a headline number and a per-incident cap to avoid outsized single-incident credits.
- For latency: we can accept an instrumented, measured SLO, but would like a hard P95 <= 300ms during 9am–6pm ET for the /reconcile route, measured across a rolling 30d window; if unavailable, remediation would be a small credit (not full availability credit).

We're okay meeting — copying procurement for availability.

-Elena

From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>
To: Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.ai>, Elena Park <elena.park@statelyfinance.com>
Cc: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.ai>
Date: Thu, 27 May 2027 08:22:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Request: availability carveouts and monthly remediation cap

Quick internal note and suggested counter to put on the table:

- We should avoid blanket 99.95% for Hosted (multi-tenant). Suggestion: 99.9% baseline for Hosted; 99.95% can be offered for Dedicated or for a committed-reserved agreement. Pricing differential to be presented in the MAP.
- Monthly remediation cap: propose a two-tiered cap — introductory period (first 6 months) capped at 20% of monthly invoice to help Stately ramp with confidence; thereafter cap reverts to 10%.
- Per-incident cap: set a hard single-incident cap at 5% of monthly invoice to avoid outsized refunds.
- Maintenance carveouts: agree to carve out scheduled batch windows if Redwood is given 7 days' notice; limit carveouts to no more than 8 hrs/week unless explicitly agreed.
- Latency SLO: willing to instrument and report P95; commit to a remediation credit that is a fraction of availability credit (e.g., 25% of the availability credit) when latency SLO is missed for the /reconcile route. Need legal to craft measurement and exclusion language (bursts, DDoS, customer misconfiguration).

Attaching a draft remediation schedule for procurement to review (remediation-schedule-draft.docx). Laura — can you confirm contract language owners?

Thanks,
Ben Carter
Director, Reliability
Redwood Inference

--
Attachment: remediation-schedule-draft.docx

From: Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.ai>
To: Elena Park <elena.park@statelyfinance.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>, Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.ai>, procurement@statelyfinance.com
Date: Sun, 30 May 2027 15:04:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Service availability guardrails & remediation cap proposal

Elena / procurement team —

Thanks all for the fast feedback. To move the account forward and keep procurement modeling simple, here's a consolidated counterproposal from Redwood:

- Availability: 99.92% monthly for Hosted accounts. 99.95% available if Stately signs a Dedicated/reserved capacity commitment (we'll provide pricing).
- Monthly remediation cap: 15% of monthly invoice (deterministic cap).
- Per-incident cap: 5% of monthly invoice (hard single-incident upper bound).
- Introductory ramp: for the first 3 billing cycles we will not increase the per-month cap above 15% (no introductory premium).
- Scheduled maintenance carveouts: allowed for your Saturday nightly batch windows provided Redwood receives 7 days' notice and carveouts are limited to a total of 6 hours per week unless mutually agreed.
- Latency: Redwood will instrument P95 for /reconcile and commit to reporting on a rolling 30d window. We propose a P95 target of 350ms (slightly higher than your 300ms ask) with a remediation equal to 25% of the availability credit when latency SLO is missed. Measurement exclusions: bursts beyond committed QPS, customer-side misconfiguration, and acts of God.

If Stately accepts these guardrails, Redwood will prepare a short SLA amendment and a MAP that lists: deployment mode, estimated monthly spend, measurement endpoints, and notification cadence. Please confirm: 1) preferred deployment (Hosted vs Dedicated), 2) approximate committed spend, and 3) a contact for DocuSign.

Proposed next step: 30-min review with procurement + legal Wed or Thu next week. Book here: https://calendly.com/redwood-sales/30min?month=2027-06

Looking forward —
Monica Patel
Enterprise Sales
Redwood Inference
